triage.note: D5 half 1, promoted from the PR #21 V5 debt row. `.split`'s `@media(max-width:1100px)` dropped `#source` to `grid-column:1/-1`, stacking it BELOW `#pane`, so under 1100px the compare pane and the item pane were never on screen together and sync-scroll had nothing to demonstrate itself against — while the control still rendered checked and live. The check pins BOTH halves of the debt row's own Why cell rather than choosing one: every stacking `@media` block must trigger strictly below `min_side_by_side` (1024), and the three expressions that carry the stacked state into the control (`syncOn` honouring `disabled`, `syncStacked` setting `disabled` AND the `#sync-state` wording, the `change` listener) are pinned WHOLE on the WIRE_UI allow-list argument. The CSS breakpoint and the JS `matchMedia` width are tied to the same number, so re-raising one without the other goes red twice.
triage.ceiling: STATIC READ. This check parses CSS and JS TEXT out of src/sec10k/web/static/index.html — no test in this harness issues an HTTP request and nothing here lays anything out, so it does NOT observe the render. It cannot see whether `#pane` and `#source` actually share a row at 1024px; it can only see that the source no longer declares the rule that stopped them. The rendered geometry is browser evidence and lives in tasks/reviews/d5-browser-walk.json (1280 / 1024 / 900 / 768). The existing pin mechanism's documented holes apply here too (a pinned element can be `hidden` and still satisfy its pin).
